config.hypothesis:
CONTEXT: We improve the policy by self-play: a challenger learns by playing a
frozen copy of the current champion (epsilon-greedy DQN, uniform replay,
negamax targets). The board and player are represented AlphaZero-style as two
6x7 planes - plane 0 the mover's pieces, plane 1 the opponent's - flipped to
the mover's perspective every move, so there is no whose-turn input. The
policy is a small conv net (2 conv layers of 32 filters, one 128-unit hidden
layer, 7 Q-value outputs). The current champion (connect4-pol-00005) has trained
for 1500 episodes and scores 0.030 on the solver ladder
(depths 1-6; 1.0 = beats every depth nearly always; its frontier - the
shallowest solver it cannot beat 90% of the time - is depth 1).

HYPOTHESIS: 1500 additional self-play episodes (5 iterations of 300), with no
other change, will raise absolute strength. The champion is early in training,
so more of the same training should still convert directly into strength.

PREDICTION: If true, we expect the final champion's ladder score to be at
least 0.09 above the incumbent's (0.030 -> 0.120),
because early-stage DQN gains scale with episodes and 0.09 is the smallest
gain our 168-game ladder evaluation can distinguish from noise.

DECISION CRITERIA (recorded so a false positive or false negative can be
traced back before it sends us down a bad path): a challenger is promoted only
if its head-to-head score against the champion clears a 95% Wilson lower bound
above 0.5 over 200 games (about a 5% chance of promoting a policy that is no
better), and promotion is blocked if its ladder score is significantly below
the champion's - the gate that catches beats-the-champion-but-weaker-in-
absolute-terms cycling. Gains smaller than 0.09 ladder / 0.06 head-to-head are
invisible at these game counts and will be recorded INCONCLUSIVE, never
refuted; the follow-up for an inconclusive result is more evaluation games,
not abandoning the direction.

CONTEXT: Same policy, representation, and learner as exp-002-more-self-play
(AlphaZero-style two-plane mover-perspective board; small conv net; DQN).

episodes produced 3 head-to-head promotions but the ladder score stayed flat

CONTEXT: We improve the policy by self-play: a challenger (epsilon-greedy DQN,
negamax targets) learns by playing a frozen copy of the current champion. The
board is two 6x7 planes - plane 0 the mover's pieces, plane 1 the opponent's -
flipped to the mover's perspective every move (no whose-turn input). The
policy is a small conv net (2x32-filter conv layers, 128-unit hidden layer,
7 Q-value outputs). The current champion (connect4-pol-00148) scores
0.071 on the solver ladder (depths 1-6; 1.0 = beats every
depth nearly always); its frontier - the shallowest solver it cannot beat 90%
of the time - is depth 1.
Evidence chain: capacity is sufficient (exp-010), endgame values are
calibrated in sign and magnitude (solver-proven wins +0.66, losses -0.67 on
the champion card), yet the champion still misses ~9% of immediate wins and
~11% of forced blocks (card: take_the_win 0.91, block_the_loss 0.89) and
cannot beat the depth-1 solver reliably (rung-1 = 0.34). Data levers are
exhausted (exp-002..009), deeper nets don't help (exp-018), and MC credit
propagation hurt (exp-019). The one structural difference between the
policy and every opponent that beats it: the policy never looks ahead.

HYPOTHESIS: reflex-only inference is the binding constraint. Wrapping the
UNCHANGED champion network in a k-ply negamax over real rules (leaves valued
by the network) raises its ladder score substantially with ZERO additional
training. Exact change: move selection argmax(Q(s,.)) -> argmax over
search-backed values at depth k in (1, 2, 3). Network weights untouched.

PREDICTION: depth-2 ladder >= 0.20 (vs bare 0.071; the
2-ply search mechanically eliminates both card-flagged blunder classes, and
rung-1 alone should approach 1.0 since a depth-1 solver can be matched by a
depth-2 search with any sane leaf values); depth-3 >= depth-2. If depth-2
stays < 0.12, the leaf values are too poor to search over, and the
bottleneck is value quality after all. Follow-on if supported: search during
TRAINING (self-play with lookahead = AlphaZero-lite), and the policy-card
'horizon' question becomes moot — the search supplies the horizon.

DECISION CRITERIA (recorded so a false positive or negative can be traced
later): promotion requires the head-to-head score's 95% Wilson lower bound to
clear 0.5 over 200 games (~5% false-promotion rate) and no statistically
significant ladder regression. The 168-game ladder cannot distinguish gains
under ~0.09 from noise: a positive-but-smaller gain is recorded INCONCLUSIVE,
never refuted - the follow-up is more evaluation games, not abandonment.

tldr: SUPPORTED, largest effect in the program: the UNCHANGED champion network (bare ladder 0.071) scores 0.089 with 1-ply lookahead, 0.217 with 2-ply (prediction >= 0.20 met), and 0.310 with 3-ply — 4.4x the bare score and 2.7x the all-time training record (0.116), with ZERO additional training. Rung-1 went 0.29 -> 0.68 at depth 3. Reflex-only inference WAS the binding constraint: the network's knowledge was good enough to search over but not good enough to act on in one glance. Frontier is still depth 1 (rung-1 0.68 < 0.90 mastery), so search alone is not mastery — but every prior lever moved the ladder by hundredths; this moved it by tenths. Cost: 96s for a depth-3 ladder eval (507k leaf evals) vs ~2s bare. NEXT: (a) make lookahead the default for evaluation/promotion so champions are judged with it; (b) search during TRAINING (self-play with lookahead = AlphaZero-lite), so the net learns from stronger play and the leaf values improve, compounding with the search.

config.hypothesis:
CONTEXT: We improve the policy by self-play: a challenger (epsilon-greedy DQN,
negamax targets) learns by playing a frozen copy of the current champion. The
board is two 6x7 planes - plane 0 the mover's pieces, plane 1 the opponent's -
flipped to the mover's perspective every move (no whose-turn input). The
policy is a small conv net (2x32-filter conv layers, 128-unit hidden layer,
7 Q-value outputs). The current champion (connect4-pol-00246) scores
0.042 on the solver ladder (depths 1-6; 1.0 = beats every
depth nearly always); its frontier - the shallowest solver it cannot beat 90%
of the time - is depth 1.
Evidence chain: exp-020 — the unchanged champion scores 0.071 bare, 0.217
with 2-ply lookahead, 0.310 with 3-ply: its knowledge is good enough to
SEARCH over but not to ACT on in one forward pass. Every training lever that
left inference untouched moved the ladder by hundredths (exp-002..019).
Recipe 3-seed bare baseline: (0.054, 0.06, 0.116) (mean 0.077, spread 0.062).

HYPOTHESIS (human-directed split: search in training, bare at evaluation):
letting the learner look ahead while practicing improves the network's
one-glance play, because (A) it trains on stronger, less blunder-filled
games, and (B — this arm's extra claim if search_targets) regressing Q onto
search-backed values distills the lookahead into the weights (expert
iteration). Exact changes vs the recipe: train_search_depth 0 -> 2;
AND search_targets True: each stored move's training target is the search-backed value of that move (supervised, done=True) instead of the one-step TD estimate; tactical shaping is NOT added on top (the search already prices the tactics). Benchmark and head-to-head: bare inference, unchanged.
This run: arm B-search-targets, seed 28.

PREDICTION (scored per arm over its three seeds, bare-inference ladder):
Arm A mean >= 0.14 (baseline mean + spread) if stronger self-play data alone
helps; Arm B mean >= 0.20 — distillation should move the bare network a
good way toward exp-020's 2-ply search score (0.217), and the policy cards'
take-the-win / block-the-loss rates should approach 1.0 since those are
exactly what a 2-ply search prices. If B <= A, the targets add nothing over
the data; if both <= baseline, search knowledge does not transfer into
one-glance weights at this scale and inference-time search becomes the
design question again. Training cost ~50x more forward passes per self-play
move — recorded, acceptable.

DECISION CRITERIA (recorded so a false positive or negative can be traced
later): promotion requires the head-to-head score's 95% Wilson lower bound to
clear 0.5 over 200 games (~5% false-promotion rate) and no statistically
significant ladder regression. The 168-game ladder cannot distinguish gains
under ~0.09 from noise: a positive-but-smaller gain is recorded INCONCLUSIVE,
never refuted - the follow-up is more evaluation games, not abandonment.

tldr: Reference arm: recipe baseline under corrected detector = 0.080/0.054/0.060 (mean 0.064). JOINT VERDICT exp-022 (9 runs, corrected plateau detector, gate v2, bare eval): recipe baseline 0.080/0.054/0.060 (mean 0.064); Arm A search-picks-moves 0.048/0.068/0.060 (mean 0.059); Arm B search-targets 0.045/0.036/0.077 (mean 0.053). Both predictions (A>=0.14, B>=0.20) FAILED: search during training did not transfer into one-glance strength. MECHANISM, from the cards: Arm B DID distill long-range value (value_horizon 33-37 plies vs ~0 baseline; Q at solver-proven wins ~1.0-1.2) but destroyed one-ply tactics (take-the-win 0.25-0.28, block 0.36-0.57 vs baseline ~0.9) and inflated the value scale (mean|Q| ~1.0, max 2.8). Interpretation: search targets bootstrap through the net's own inflated leaf values, so non-winning moves also get near-+1 targets and the ordering collapses. Card-driven fix candidate: bound leaf/target values to [-1,1] (clip or tanh head) before distilling. Also: under gate v2 the baseline seed32 promoted pol-00246 at ladder 0.042 via the relative path — the champion ratchet (0.083->0.071->0.042) the strict gate (ADR-007) now prevents.
